name: EU Digital Travel Application Regulation
evidence_rating: ex-ante only: detailed LFS uptake targets; small pilot evidence cited by the Commission; proposal pending
summary: The Commission wants an EU app that lets travellers send a digital copy of their passport before crossing Schengen's external borders, with targets of 30% of travellers using it within five years of launch (planned for end 2030). It expects faster, safer border checks at modest cost, about EUR 2 million per country and EUR 49.5 million for the EU app, Pilots in Finland and Croatia cut border processing of pre-cleared travellers from 30-90 seconds to under 9 seconds, but the EU-wide effect cannot be measured until the app exists.

literature.citation: European Commission (2024), Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal establishing an application for the electronic submission of travel data (EU Digital Travel application), SWD(2024) 671 (executive summary SWD(2024) 672)
literature.title: Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal establishing an application for the electronic submission of travel data (EU Digital Travel application)
literature.outcomes: border security; waiting times; public costs
literature.headline: Preferred option (mandatory acceptance of DTCs) has highest expected uptake and allows advance checks; costs: about EUR 2m per Member State on average (pilots: EUR 300,000-700,000 plus up to EUR 250,000 servers), eu-LISA EUR 49.5m one-off to 2031 and ~20 FTE; time savings not monetised; EU-funded DTC pilots cut processing of pre-cleared travellers from 30-90 seconds to under 9 seconds
literature.summary_plain: The Commission expected a common EU travel app for digital passports to speed up border checks and improve security, at about EUR 2 million per country plus EUR 49.5 million for the EU agency that would build it.
